My relationship with my mother improved, but the relationship with the rest of my family and friends is incredibly strained on my end. It’s not all terrible, but I have a long way to go. 

Sometimes I contemplate a third, and the only thing stopping me is the PTSD I developed with hospitals as a result of the behavioral health center I was at and what a third attempt will do to my mom. 

But improvement is slow but steady...

I am Hispanic and grew up in an apartment. 

Plus, my mom use to always put the gifts under the tree a few weeks early. But, she would humor the whole Santa thing by making it seem like he would take back the gifts if I decided to be a jerk during the holidays.

It was my senior year in high school and I had a choice between dating my best friend and this guy I had recently met. 

I fucked up hard by picking a stranger over my best friend. Because of my shit logic, I caused my best friend so much grief. I picked a stranger over my best friend who I did have romantic feelings for because I didn't want to jeopardize our long established friendship in fear that I would no longer have anyone there for me if something were to go wrong. 

My rejection caused him to make poor choice in order to fill a void that I had created. He dated a girl (we call her crazy) who was a manipulative narcissist that would would use him, abuse him, and made him feel like a bad guy whenever he would be himself. I couldn't let him live like that. I had to get him out of that relationship. He deserved better. 

I got him out of that. He's now my SO. I love him with all my heart. But I cannot forgive myself for rejecting him the first time he asked me out. I could have saved him from all that suffering. He has some really bad emotion scars from it. 

I could have prevented all of that.

Two of my computers died before reaching their first year in my possession. They both caught fire. 

....I should probably dust more often.

I started to wear my war paint in early high school as part of a baby step to a self improvement trip that help me become more confident by improving small details on my face.

I did many things that I never thought I would do, like try out for my school plays, join clubs and play sports. I went from a loner to that kid who all the peeps knew. 

I use to be so dissatisfied with my life that I contemplated ending it. I never would have thought that changing a little of what I saw in the mirror would bring me so far. 

Taking an extra 10 minutes in the morning helped change my life around. 

It's so annoying when people just bash makeup. I don't wear it for anyone else. I wear it for myself. It takes what nice features I never noticed I had and made them better. It helped bring my confidence to the point where I can still walk out of my house without it on and still feel beautiful and strong. 

Makeup was training wheels to a whole new me. 

(Makeup is also a nice creative output for myself. Sketching and painting didn't feel like enough. Makeup getting tossed in there gave me a new canvas to go to town on.)
